feature: The video clickthroughs say the same thing the video design says
summary: All fifteen video mock pages now open a Layers list at the top of the dock, listing exactly the rows the timeline shows in the same order with the same icons, and no page asks you to type a clip's start, end or length into a box any more.
setup: The design dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791. Open the Video section; every page under it is in this pass. Nothing to switch on.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#video and look at the right-hand dock.
Read the five names in Layers against the five rows on the strip below: same names, same order, same icons.
Click any row in Layers and watch the clip on the strip light up, and the other way round.
Open the Panels list at the bottom of the dock and try to switch Layers off.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#video-cut-wt and step to 'Get the sound out of the picture'.
Watch Layers go from one to two at the moment the voice-over becomes its own layer, and a row appear on the strip to match.
Read the Clip section in the panel: Reads, Volume, Speed, and nowhere to type a start or an end.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#video-speed and look under the strip: the before-and-after of a retime is two bars on one scale now, not two fake timeline rows.

evaluate: With Layers back, does the dock read as one place with a job, or does it feel like the timeline and the list are saying the same thing twice?
A clip's start and end are now only on the strip. Is that a relief or does something feel missing when you want the exact number?
On the transitions page nothing in Layers ever lights up, because a cut is not a layer. Does the list read as broken there, or as correctly quiet?
The main sequence row is called 'Story' on the pages that lay shots end to end. Is that a name you would recognise, or should the row take the name of the first clip on it?
Layers costs the panel about 130 points in every video document. Watching Properties scroll sooner, is that trade worth it?
rough: Layers takes real room and the panel pays for it. On video-transition-wt the Properties group now scrolls with a row cut in half at the fold. That is the dock's normal behaviour and it is the exact arithmetic video-surface.md §4 names (a 968 point panel with 733 left once the strip is open), but it is the first thing a reviewer will point at.

A transition's Length and a dip's Hold on black are still numbers you pick in the panel. I kept them: they are rows with a way in, the same shape as Volume, not a grid of number boxes, and they are not a clip's in, out or duration. If the rule is meant to cover them too, they are two one-line changes.

video-transition-wt's main row is now called Story rather than V1, following video.html, which already used that name for a row of shots laid end to end. Nobody has settled whether a storyline row should be called Story or take the name of the first clip on it.

video-speed lost its Source and Retimed rows, which were never layers. The before-and-after comparison they were really drawing now sits under the strip as two bars on one scale, which is smaller and, I think, clearer, but it is a change away from what the page drew.

The Panels list in the dock used to let you switch Layers off, which the app cannot do (PanelSectionVisibility.optionalSections deliberately does not list Layers). I made required panes list without a switch across the whole study, not just the video pages. That touches every page with a dock; the gates are green and thirteen sample pages render clean, but it is wider than this task.
